name: Black Hole
definition: A region in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that nothing, including light, can escape.

size.diameter: typically between 10 and 30 kilometers (6 and 19 miles)
size.mass: can be millions or even billions of times more massive than the sun

types: Stellar Black Hole (formed from the collapse of a massive star)
Supermassive Black Hole (found at the center of galaxies)
Intermediate-Mass Black Hole (with masses that fall between stellar and supermassive black holes)

properties.gravity: so strong that it warps space-time
properties.event_horizon: the point of no return, where the gravity is so strong that anything that crosses it will be trapped
properties.temperature: increases as matter falls towards the black hole
properties.emission: can emit radiation, including X-rays and gamma rays, due to the hot accretion disk surrounding it

history.discovery: first proposed by John Michell in 1783
history.modernUnderstanding: developed by David Finkelstein in 1958 and Roger Penrose in 1965

interesting_facts.singularity: the center of a black hole is thought to be a point of infinite density and zero volume
interesting_facts.cosmic_ray: some black holes are thought to be responsible for the origin of cosmic rays
interesting_facts.star_suck: supermassive black holes can affect the orbits of stars and even entire galaxies
